leading_positions.synthesis: Four of eight members include targeted protein degradation (PROTACs and molecular glues) in their preferred configuration, short of the five-vote majority. Aqvist, Brzezinski and Linke name the same trio (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) with near-identical citations about small molecules recruiting E3 ligases. Chabes supports B027 only as a second prize part, with Crews and Handa but not Deshaies, paired with Liu's base editing (B038). Shared: the induced-proximity mechanism is clear, independently reproduced, and a new modality. Not shared: whether a single citation can span the PROTAC and cereblon/glue branches, whether Deshaies is indispensable, and whether the absence of an approved degrader makes the prize early. Linke moved his third name from Ciulli to Handa after hearing colleagues; Ciulli, Sakamoto, Ito and Gray remain outside every preferred trio.

Two members prefer ionizable lipid nanoparticles for nucleic-acid delivery, and both now name Cullis, Madden and Hope (Aili moved from Cullis, Anderson, MacLachlan after Sparr's argument). Shared: the pKa-tuned, self-assembly-based design principle is chemistry, clinical impact is already proven and independently validated, and overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize concerns the mRNA cargo rather than the carrier. Not shared by the wider committee: Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Somfai and Zou doubt that three names from six credited (Cullis, Madden, Hope, MacLachlan, Anderson, Langer) can be chosen defensibly, and some see formulation rather than chemistry. Aili concedes his trio omits later optimisation and siRNA translation, which is where Anderson and MacLachlan matter.

Chabes prefers base editing as a single-laureate part (David R. Liu), alongside B027. Aqvist lists B038 as an alternative with the same Liu-only view and Somfai lists it as an alternative. Shared by those who discuss it: the deaminase chemistry and Liu's attribution are clean. Not shared: timing against a short clinical record, the 2020 CRISPR prize as framing, and the parallel Target-AID claim of Nishida and Kondo. Brzezinski and Aili would hold it for a later year.

Somfai alone prefers Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig), citing a mature, mechanistically explained method with two-person attribution. Linke lists it as an alternative. Others raise that the 2010 cross-coupling prize may make it read as an extension, and that the Kosugi/Migita tin-amide precedent needs acknowledgement. Somfai argues C-N coupling posed a distinct mechanistic problem requiring new ligand design.

Zou alone prefers halide perovskite solar absorbers (Snaith, Park, Miyasaka). In the opening Linke and Brzezinski ranked it fifth and sixth. Zou rests the case on structure-property links and independent confirmation. Open objections are stability, lead content and scale-up, and the exclusion of Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis. No other member lists B066 in a round-1 preferred configuration or as an alternative.

areas_of_agreement: Targeted protein degradation (B027) is the only ballot in the preferred configuration of four members and in the alternatives of three more (Somfai, Sparr, Zou), and all eight accept that its induced-proximity mechanism is chemically clear and independently reproduced.

Crews and Deshaies as originators of the PROTAC concept, and Handa for the cereblon identification, are the names that Aqvist, Brzezinski and Linke each give in their preferred B027 trio; Chabes also includes Crews and Handa.
Base editing attribution is cleanest for David R. Liu alone according to Chabes and Aqvist; no other member proposes a different laureate set for B038.

Several members state that the 2023 Medicine prize overlap for lipid nanoparticles concerns mRNA nucleoside modification rather than the carrier chemistry, and treat it as a framing issue, not a blocker (Aili, Sparr, Linke).
Members agree that attribution for B062 is the hardest on the shortlist, with six credited names for three places.
scientific_disputes: Whether lipid nanoparticles count as chemistry: Aili and Sparr argue pKa-tuned ionizable lipid design and bilayer/non-bilayer phase behaviour are physical chemistry, while Aqvist, Somfai and Zou see largely empirical formulation or insufficiently understood structure-activity rules.

Whether C-N coupling (B019) is a distinct achievement or a refinement of the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize: Somfai says the amine-coordination and reductive-elimination problems demanded new ligand design; Linke is not yet convinced it is distinct.

Whether biomolecular condensates (B050) are mature: Sparr, Brzezinski, Chabes and Linke raise concerns that functional liquid condensates in cells are unproven and rest on overexpression imaging, with Pappu and Mittag omitted from a Hyman/Brangwynne/Rosen trio.

Whether base editing is a new chemical principle or an application of the CRISPR platform recognised in 2020, and whether Car-Parrinello (B049) or Gray-Winkler (B026) differ enough from prizes already given in computation (1998, 2013) and electron transfer (1992).
Whether the nitrogenase (B043) catalytic mechanism is settled enough to write a defensible citation; Brzezinski and Zou accept that structures are settled but the mechanism is not.
attribution_disputes: B027: whether the third name is Handa (Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke, Chabes) or Ciulli, and whether Deshaies is dropped (Chabes) or retained. The opening files showed Linke and Sparr with Ciulli; Sakamoto, Ito, Kim and Gray are also credited but in no preferred trio.

B062: Aili and Sparr now share Cullis, Madden, Hope, but the openings also proposed Anderson, MacLachlan and Langer (Aili, Zou); Brzezinski, Chabes, Somfai and Zou note that differing trios signal unsettled credit. The question is whether the citation honours early encapsulation and ionizable-lipid principle or later library discovery and clinical siRNA delivery.
B038: Liu alone versus adding Nishida and Kondo (Target-AID).
B019: whether Kosugi's tin-amide precedent warrants a third laureate or only acknowledgement.
B066: Snaith, Park, Miyasaka versus Gratzel, Seok, Kanatzidis; B043: Dean and Ribbe versus Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt.
maturity_disputes: No degrader is approved according to the members who comment (Linke, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Aili, Sparr, Somfai), so B027 is judged either early by some or sufficiently confirmed in mechanism by others; clinical status is described from memory and unverified.
Base editing has roughly a decade of clinical history and, per Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski and Somfai, a short record against lipid nanoparticles, which are already proven in patients.
Perovskites (B066) have unresolved long-term stability, lead content and scale-up; Zou argues the criterion is scientific confirmation, not commercial maturity.
Condensates (B050) and nitrogenase mechanism are described as still debated; Car-Parrinello and Pd C-N coupling are described as unambiguously mature.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Eight members state that no specific conflict or recusal need is apparent from their profiles for any preferred candidate.
Zou states that her field of 3D electron diffraction is adjacent to serial femtosecond crystallography (B002) and would treat that ballot cautiously; B002 is in no member's preferred configuration.

Sparr discloses that lipid self-assembly is her own research area, giving scientific closeness to B062 and B050 but no personal tie to a credited person; Aili notes a general overlap with Sparr in peptide and self-assembly research.
Chabes notes that his nucleotide-metabolism and DNA-replication-fidelity background is adjacent to B038 and B027 and may shape his view, with no direct collaboration.

Collegial links disclosed without bearing on candidates: Linke, Somfai and Sparr are Lund colleagues; Brzezinski and Zou are Stockholm University colleagues; Linke chairs as a physicist and is a B027 supporter.
questions_for_round2: For B027, should the citation cover both the PROTAC and cereblon/glue branches, and if three names are required, is it Crews, Deshaies and Handa, or does the committee prefer Ciulli, or a split structure that Chabes's two-person Crews/Handa version illustrates?

Does the committee consider the absence of an approved degrader a reason to defer B027, and what evidence of clinical or tool validation, stated by members from the record rather than memory, would resolve it?

For B062, can Aili and Sparr state which discovery the citation honours (early encapsulation and ionizable-lipid principle versus later lipid-library discovery and siRNA delivery), and can they justify Cullis, Madden and Hope over Anderson, MacLachlan and Langer?
Can Aili, Sparr and Zou say how the chemistry content of B062 and its distance from the 2023 Medicine prize would be written into a citation that a non-specialist can follow?
Would Chabes support B027 as a sole prize part, or only paired with B038, and does the committee prefer one coherent achievement or a two-part prize pairing different fields?
Is Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B019) a distinct achievement from the 2010 prize, and how would a citation acknowledge Kosugi and Migita?
Do members preferring B019, B038, B062 or B066 regard B027 as acceptable, and if so on what condition, so the committee can see whether any configuration can reach five votes?
summary.chair_observation: No configuration has the five votes needed. B027 has four explicit supporters, B062 two, and B038, B019 and B066 one each; Chabes's two-part configuration counts under both B038 and B027. The B027 trio converged on Crews, Deshaies and Handa after discussion, but Chabes omits Deshaies, and the shared objections across the eight files are attribution crowding and the absence of an approved degrader. Several alternatives (B050, B043, B026, B049, B052, B012, B002, B022) were listed by members but are not in any preferred configuration. This summary records stated positions only and is not a ruling.
